text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
AUSTRALIA, July 21 - COAL - QUEENSLAND - Abbot Point - One vessel loading, 1 waiting, 4 due by 27/7, no delays.

Hay Point - Notice has been given with respect to the terminal upgrade and revised restrictions as follows, stockpile upgrade to commence this week with expected completion in February 1998. The terminal is upgrading stacker and reclaimer capacity in the stockpile area. During the upgrade, expected delays due to reduced reclaimer rates will reduce ship loading to approx. 2,500 mt/hr when 2 vessels are loading at the 2 berths. Further delays may occur due to coal blending on certain shipments. On completion of the stockpile upgrade the expected load rates at each berths will be approx. 5,000 mt/hr. Berth no. 2 will be closed for maintenance from 17/11 to 19/12. Air draft in berth No.1 has been restated to 23 metres less tide (instead of 22 metres less tide). Depth alongside berth No.1 has been remeasured to 15.6 metres at lat (from 16.0 metres lat). Depth alongside berth No.2 has been remeasured to 16.4 metres at lat (from 16.8 metres lat). One vessel loading, 2 waiting, 9 due by 2/8, no delays.
Dalrymple Bay - Two vessels loading, 1 waiting, 39 due by 10/9, no delays.
Gladstone - Curragh strike now in its 10th week. Negotiations continue. R.G. Tanna - 2 Vessels loading, 3 waiting, 24 due by 20/9, no delays.
Barney Point - Berth vacant, 6 vessels due by 25/8, no delays.
Brisbane - Berth vacant, 4 vessels due by 2/8, no delays.

NEW SOUTH WALES - Newcastle - Miners at Hunter Valley No.1 mine accepted a union recommendation at 0800 hrs. 22/7 to return to work at midnight following private talks in the Australian Industrial Relations Commission overnight. The first train was loaded at 1100 hrs. 22/7, using union labour and a second train was ready to load. The first train has not yet arrived at the loading terminal. However, there is no indication of likely problems at the terminal now that union labour has been used to load the trains. Under the peace plan set up by the IRC's coal panel, a 21 day negotiation period will be set down for talks between the parties. During this period, the mine owners will take staff off the operations side, and the union will remove the pickets.
Kooragang - 3 Vessels loading, 20 waiting, 8 due by 27/7, 15-16 days delay. Dyke 4 - 3 Vessels loading, 16 waiting, 4 due by 27/7, 14-15 days delay.

Port Kembla - One vessel loading, 3 waiting, 17 due by 28/8. Delays are due to vessels berthing out of turn due to awaiting cargo. Tug crews (members of Maritime Union of Australia) employed by Wallace tugs, walked off the job at 1430 hrs. 21/7 in connection with their EBA, they met 22/7 at 0700 hrs. and have decided to remain off the job until the next meeting scheduled for 0700 hrs. 23/7. No shipping movements since 1430 hrs. 21/7.

IRON ORE - WESTERN AUSTRALIA - Port Hedland - Mt. Newman (Nelson Point) - Situation remains unchanged regarding shortage of lump and yandi fines. Berth A - 1 Vessel berthed, 3 anchored. Berth B - 1 Vessel loading, 3 anchored. 13 Vessels due by 30/7, 8 others due by 24/8.
Goldsworthy (Finucane Island) - 1 Vessel loading, 2 anchored, 1 due 22/7, 3 others due with no eta.
Dampier - Parker Point - 1 Vessel loading, 4 anchored.
E.I. Island - 1 Vessel loading, 4 anchored, 1 due 21/7.
Dampier lineup - 4 Vessels anchored, 19 due by 7/8.
Port Walcott - One vessel loading, 14 due by 10/8.
